The one thing that matters most

Google DeepMind released Genie 4, a world model that builds a game-like 3D world from a text prompt in real time, with sound and characters who talk, and lets you change it as you walk around.

Early testers showed it making cities, a DOOM-filled office and a flying mouse on the spot; it is rolling out to trusted testers first. Also big: Grok Bot 0.77.0 shipped and Anthropic said Claude is now doing drug discovery work.

Users can now prompt changes to the world dynamically and generate worlds with native audio.

It is rolling out to Trusted Testers as a research preview and will soon come to Google AI Ultra subscribers and early access partners via the Gemini API and AI Studio.

Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index version 5 is live: Claude Opus 5.5 leads at 58, ahead of GPT-6 Astra at 57 and GPT-6.1 Sol at 55; Gemini 4 Argon is next at 50.

🚨 AI News | TestingCatalog@testingcatalog
Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 is now live!

> It includes 2 new benchmarks and 3 upgrades, and most of the Index is built on private datasets.

> New benchmarks include FrontierCode 2.0 from Cognition and Terminal-Bench-Science.

> Claude Opus 5.5 (max) leads at 58, ahead of GPT-6 Astra (max, 57) and GPT-6.1 Sol (max, 55): Anthropic and OpenAI hold the top five models. Gemini 4 Argon (high) is next at 50.

Claude Code still remains in the lead (no surprise here), while we have quite an accurate distribution for the rest.

A new chart also shows model release dates 👀
Artificial Analysis@ArtificialAnlys· Oct 27
Announcing Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5, featuring 2 new benchmarks and 3 upgrades. For the first time, the majority of the Index is built on private datasets

The Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index is our composite measure of model capabilities across tasks reflecting real-world usage today. v5 is our biggest upgrade since v4 launched in January. With v5, 60% of the Index is now based on evaluations with private test sets or held-out answers.

Alongside Intelligence Index v5, we’re launching the Artificial Analysis Progress Index v1, which tracks model capability over time on one continuous scale.

New to the Intelligence Index:

➤ FrontierCode 2.0: Cognition's newly-launched private benchmark of real-world coding tasks, graded on whether a repository maintainer would merge the agent's change

➤ Terminal-Bench-Science: 70 agentic scientific research tasks, run in a terminal environment

Upgraded:

➤ HLE-Diamond (replacing Humanity's Last Exam): a refined 1,000-question version of Humanity's Last Exam, split evenly between reasoning and knowledge questions

➤ AA-Omniscience v1.1: An updated dataset with saturated and public set questions removed, new questions added, and ambiguous or erroneous questions revised

➤ CritPt v2: a private, 40-question hard subset of CritPt v2, revised by the CritPt authors and run with a code-execution tool

Staying in the Index: AA-Briefcase, AutomationBench-AA, GDP.pdf and Terminal-Bench 4.0

Removed from the Index: GDPval-AA v2.1, SciCode, and AA-LCR v1.1

Key results:

➤ Claude Opus 5.5 (max) leads at 58, ahead of GPT-6 Astra (max, 57) and GPT-6.1 Sol (max, 55): Anthropic and OpenAI hold the top five models. Gemini 4 Argon (high) is next at 50

➤ The open weights gap widens from 3 points to 12: Kimi K3.1 Pro (weights not yet released) is the top open weights model at 46. Among released weights, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (max) and GLM-5.3 (max) lead at 32 - 26 points behind the leader and below Claude Haiku 5.5 (max, 36)

➤ Cost per task varies by more than 13x among the leading models: of the 10 highest-scoring models shown, GPT-6.1 Terra (max) is the cheapest at $0.96 per Intelligence Index task and Claude Fable 5.1 (max) the most expensive at $13.04

Axiom's agents turned a 15,000-page math proof that took 100 mathematicians decades into about 43 million lines of machine-checkable code in 24 days.

🚨 AI News | TestingCatalog@testingcatalog
Axiom released an open-source GitHub repo where dozens of AI agents turned a 15,000-page math proof into about 43 million lines of code in 24 days.

The proof, known as the Classification of Finite Simple Groups, took 100 mathematicians several decades and lists every basic building block of symmetry in mathematics.

The code is written in Lean, a programming language that checks every step of a proof, allowing the whole result to be verified by running the code instead of rereading hundreds of papers.

Axiom's chart tracks how large AI-written Lean projects have grown since mid-2025, roughly doubling every 37 days by its estimate, with this project reaching 43 million lines.
Leo@biosemiote· Oct 27
The formal proof of CFSG may now be among the largest open-source projects ever. Watching agents assemble it is a reminder of the awe-inspiring human achievement behind it. The graph represents some 15,000 pages of intricate arguments developed by mathematicians over decades.
